subject: Tidewater — post-demo stakeholder map & procurement gates
summary: Post-demo recap with stakeholder mapping (economic buyer, security, legal, procurement), requested security evidence, and a proposed procurement timeline + next meeting slots.
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@tidewater.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tidewater — post-demo stakeholder map & procurement gates

Alex — great to meet this morning, thanks for the time. Quick written recap and proposed next steps from the demo so your buying team has a concise artifact to work from.

Key takeaways (from demo):
- Use case: embed Redwood inference into Tidewater’s analytics product for natural-language summarization and guided query suggestions.
- Success metrics: reduce time-to-insight for analysts by 30% (measured via query completion rate + downstream task completion).
- Latency requirement: 200–400ms p95 for short queries; budget-sensitive for bulk batch scoring.

Stakeholder map (as discussed):
- Economic buyer: Alex Johnson (CFO) — final signoff on spend and contract length.
- Procurement lead: procurement@tidewater.com — PO & vendor setup.
- Legal: Elena Gomez — contract redlines and standard security addenda.
- Security/IT: Priya Shah — technical security review (SOC2, data handling, network controls).
- Product/Engineering sponsor: internal product lead (TBD) — integration owner for the pilot.

Immediate asks / open items from Tidewater:
1) Priya requested our SOC2 report and a populated security checklist (I attached a blank checklist and our SOC2 summary).
2) Procurement wants a preliminary pricing sheet for a 3-month pilot + options for annual commit pricing.
3) Legal will want standard data and IP language; Elena indicated she may propose a few redlines.

Proposed next steps (suggested owners and timing):
- Logan: send SOC2 summary + filled security checklist by EOD today (ACTION: Logan).
- Marissa: provide pricing matrix for pilot vs annual commit + sample SOW language (ACTION: Marissa) — target by EOD Thursday.
- Karthik: open hubspot deal with procurement checklist and link to Drive folder (ACTION: Karthik) — target by tomorrow.
- Joint: 30-minute procurement + security sync with Priya and procurement@tidewater.com — propose Wed/Fri next week.

Attachments: redwood-post-demo-summary.pdf (this doc), estimated-pricing-sheet.xlsx (placeholder).

If this looks right, I’ll push the SOC2 doc now and Marissa will follow up on pricing.

Thanks — looking forward to keeping momentum.

—
Logan Wright
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0102

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@tidewater.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@tidewater.com, Priya Shah <priya.shah@tidewater.com>, Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@tidewater.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tidewater — post-demo stakeholder map & procurement gates

Logan — thanks for the recap. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Priya and I need the SOC2 Type II report and a completed version of the security checklist (I attached our internal checklist we usually send to vendors). Can you confirm how long it will take to get those back to us?

2) Procurement (copied) will need an estimated cost for a 3-month pilot (500k tokens/month, plus up to 200k batch scoring) and a separate annual committed pricing example. Please include token pricing and any expected ancillary charges (e.g., dedicated capacity, storage, network).

3) On the timeline: we’re aiming to make a vendor recommendation to the steering committee on Oct 5. That means we need legal + security sign-off by Sep 28 to get procurement paperwork in place.

4) Legal (Elena) — can you confirm if Tidewater requires any additional clauses (e.g., vendor access to logs, data residency) up front so we can flag them with Redwood?

Attached: tidewater-saaS-security-checklist.docx (our internal template).

If you can get SOC2 + checklist back by end of day tomorrow, that will keep us on track. Thanks.

—
Alex Johnson
CFO, Tidewater Analytics
alex.johnson@tidewater.com

Alex / procurement team — looping in procurement details and a suggested path to shorten timelines.

Short procurement playbook for pilot:
- Step 1 (Vendor onboarding): we can provide a W-9, insurance cert, and standard vendor form within 2 business days once procurement shares their vendor intake link.
- Step 2 (Pilot SOW): 1–2 page SOW + acceptance criteria (we'll draft; you review). Target turnaround: 3 business days after we send draft.
- Step 3 (PO / Net terms): typical enterprise is Net 30; can discuss Net 45 for pilots if needed.

Also: pricing note — we can offer a pilot pricing cap for the 3-month pilot (not to exceed $X) that makes the approval easier. I'll attach a draft pricing matrix and a quick SOW example.

Proposed times for the procurement + security sync (30 min):
- Wed, Sep 23 at 10:00am PT
- Thu, Sep 24 at 2:30pm PT
- Fri, Sep 25 at 9:00am PT

Please confirm which slot works and Priya if you want the technical deep-dive to include our head of security (happy to add them).

Attachments: estimated-pricing-sheet.xlsx, sample-sow-1pager.docx (in Drive link).

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
